title: Raclin Murphy Museum of Art opens Mimmo Paladino exhibition
summary: The Raclin Murphy Museum of Art announces the landmark exhibition of internationally acclaimed Italian artist Mimmo Paladino (b. 1948). A leading figure of the Italian avant-garde, Paladino’s paintings, sculptures, installations, films, prints, and illustrations are held in renowned public and private collections worldwide, including at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, Tate Modern, and the Vatican Museums. He is also highly regarded for his site-specific commissions, which include the mosaic, stained-glass, and wall drawings of the Mary, Queen of Families Chapel at the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art. An overview of Paladino’s career will introduce audiences to the artist’s repertoire and highlight his position within the currents of art history through his paintings and sculptures. title: Morphy's Sept. 24 Fine Jewelry & Watches auction offers 357 superlative lots
summary: An incredible Oscar Heyman orange and yellow fancy colored diamond necklace, a rare and important Bvlgari Serpenti Jaeger-LeCoultre 18K gold diamond bracelet with a secret watch, and a 1959 Rolex GMT-Master gilt Bakelite “Pepsi” wristwatch are all expected to surpass six figures in Morphy’s Fine Jewelry & Watches auction planned for September 24, live and online. title: An exceptional two-handled urn marked Royal Worcester realizes $15,600 at Woody Auction
summary: An exceptional pedestal two-handled urn marked Royal Worcester soared to $15,600; a paperweight vase signed “L.C.T.” (Louis Comfort Tiffany) went for $11,500; and a 100-piece sterling silver flatware set by Reed and Barton in the Francis I pattern brought $9,200 at a Multi-Genre Antique Auction held August 22nd by Woody Auction. The auction was held online and live in the Woody auction hall located at 130 East 3rd Street in Douglass, and featured over 340 lots of quality antiques, as well as consignments pulled from 18 curated collections located across the United States. title: Ordovas presents Matilde de Oliveira Roque solo exhibition Stills
summary: From 1 to 5 September 2026, Ordovas presents a solo exhibition by Matilde de Oliveira Roque, the winner of the 2025 Valerie Beston Artists’ Trust Award. This year marks the 20th anniversary of the award. The Valerie Beston Artists’ Trust was established in 2006 after the death of Valerie Beston (1922-2005) who was renowned for supporting and nurturing the careers of many of the leading artists working in London throughout her extraordinary fifty-year career, including Frank Auerbach, Francis Bacon and Lucian Freud. The charity was established to support artists at the beginning of their careers; it has since collaborated with the Royal College of Art to award an annual prize to a postgraduate student selected from its degree show. title: Fotomuseum aan het Vrijthof presents Eve Arnold retrospective All about Eve
summary: Fotomuseum aan het Vrijthof in Maastricht, the Netherlands, presents a tribute to the life and work of the legendary American photojournalist Eve Arnold (1912-2012) from 19 September 2026 until 31 January 2027. The large retrospective exhibition All about Eve features a selection of 130 iconic black-and-white and colour photographs from her impressive oeuvre, with a focus on the 1950s, 1960s, and 1970s. Eve Arnold is one of the most important photographers of the 20th century. In 1951, she became the first woman to join the prestigious Magnum Photos agency. Arnold was born in Philadelphia, lived in New York City, and moved to London in 1962. The photojournalist enjoys international acclaim for her social documentary and intimate celebrity photography. The exhibition shows portraits of famous film stars such as Marilyn Monroe, Marlene Dietrich, and Joan Crawford. Works have also been selected from the series A Baby’s Momentous First

title: Nationalmuseum in Stockholm acquires unknown painting by Lavinia Fontana
summary: Nationalmuseum has purchased a previously unknown artwork by the Italian Renaissance artist Lavinia Fontana. Fontana was one of the most successful Italian painters working in the late 16th and early 17th centuries and is considered one of the first professional woman painters. The painting is an altarpiece depicting the mystical marriage of Saint Catherine of Alexandria. The altarpiece by the Italian artist Lavinia Fontana has belonged to an Italian private collection since the late nineteenth century and has therefore previously been unknown to the art world. The work was painted in 1607 and is remarkable for the exceptional quality that Fontana, at the height of her career, achieved through her complete mastery of form and colour. title: Christie's to auction Françoise Lambert collection to benefit Palace of Versailles
summary: Held twice a year across three global art market capitals, Christie's Collections Paris | London | New York auction returns for a new edition in the fall of 2026. A highlight of the Paris leg of the auction, which will be held online from September 18 to October 1, the sale of Mrs. Françoise Lambert's collection will benefit the Société des Amis de Versailles. This collection brings together old and modern paintings, antiques, 18th-century French silverware, as well as an interesting selection of furniture and chairs designed by Gourdin, Jacob, Sené, Leleu, and Riesener, among others. This collection, with an estimated value approaching one million euros, complements Mrs. Lambert's bequest for the refurnishing of the Palace of Versailles. As the sole beneficiary of Mrs. Lambert's estate, the Société des Amis de Versailles has, since its founding in 1907, worked to involve the general public in the preservation and vitality of the château de Versailles. title: Restoration of Baroque Saint Anne Chapel nears completion at San Pantalon
summary: The Chapel of Saint Anne, the first chapel off the right nave, is among the most sumptuous interiors in the church of San Pantalon. Dating to the late 17th-century renovations of the church, the chapel stands as a testament to female artistic patronage. It was commissioned by the Compagnia delle Nobildonne Devote a Sant'Anna, a lay confraternity of Venetian noblewomen dedicated to Saint Anne, the mother of the Virgin Mary. Its dazzling ensemble of colored marbles and magnificent sculptures and reliefs ranks among the finest examples of the Venetian Baroque. Over the past year, conservators from the Uni.S.Ve. firm worked to address many condition issues that were endangering the chapel's preservation. title: Galerie Urs Meile presents Rebekka Steiger exhibition Horsehair takes a long time to burn
summary: Galerie Urs Meile will present Horsehair takes a long time to burn, a solo exhibition by Swiss artist Rebekka Steiger (b. 1993, Zurich). Developed following a seven-month residency in Beijing, which concluded this March, the exhibition brings together a new group of paintings and, for the first time, six photographs. In these works animals, landscape, memory, and mortality merge into unstable, emotionally charged scenes. Steiger has drawn inspiration from China and its culture since her first residency there in 2018. During her most recent stay, the horse - a recurring figure throughout her practice - took on renewed significance. Inspired by the Year of the Fire Horse, which began this past February, Steiger’s new works draw on its association with energy, independence, endurance, and loyalty, but also with restlessness and impulsiveness. title: Galleria Barovier&Toso presents Peter Kogler's inaugural Murano glass exhibition
summary: Galleria Barovier&Toso (Murano, Venice) returns to Palazzo Barovier&Toso in Murano with a solo exhibition by Peter Kogler, on view from 10 September 2026 to 21 February 2027. The exhibition continues the gallery's programme of inviting internationally renowned artists to engage with glass for the first time, creating new works through a close collaboration with Murano's master glassmakers. "It was our friend Hans-Peter Wipplinger, Director of the Leopold Museum in Vienna, who first suggested the name of Peter Kogler, during a visit with our gallery's director Dr Mara Hofmann. The idea struck us immediately: Kogler's visual language of endlessly repeating tubes, creating infinite networks, felt like an unmistakable echo of filigrana, one of Murano's oldest techniques, in which fine threads of glass are twisted and drawn into intricate line patterns. title: Musée de Valence to open Amélie Bertrand solo exhibition Neon Club
summary: Continuing its program of monographic exhibitions devoted to contemporary artists—including Gerda Steiner & Jörg Lenzlinger (2019), Philippe Favier (2021), Hervé Di Rosa (2022), and Jaume Plensa (2024)—the Musée de Valence reaffirms its commitment to contemporary creation by inviting Amélie Bertrand to develop an original project bringing together recent works, some of which have been influenced by the museum’s architecture and collections. Through a painting practice defined by a flawlessly smooth finish, Amélie Bertrand (b. 1985) departs from idealized landscapes inspired by nature to construct settings suspended between dream and nightmare. Her compositions are meticulously built from interlocking planes and surfaces that give way to skewed perspectives and depthless horizons. title: Galerie Thomas Schulte presents Katharina Sieverding exhibition Life-Death
summary: For Berlin Art Week 2026, Galerie Thomas Schulte presents the exhibition Life–Death by Katharina Sieverding. At the heart of the exhibition is the 1969 film of the same name, complemented by large-format film stills. Created in what was then West Berlin, the work reflects an early period in the artist’s practice and a historical moment of concentrated political, social, and aesthetic upheaval. Notably, Life–Death was shown at documenta 5 in Kassel in 1972—an early marker of its art-historical significance. Within Sieverding’s filmic output, Life–Death holds a singular position. The work was shot on 16mm film during a period that was both personally and artistically formative. At the time, Sieverding was a student of Joseph Beuys at the Staatliche Kunstakademie Düsseldorf, witnessing firsthand the institutional conflicts and protest movements of the late 1960s. title: Museum of Contemporary Art Detroit showcases civic tech installation by rootoftwo
summary: How do we imagine and shape the futures increasingly being designed for us? In Anyspace? Whatever., rootoftwo examines the technological systems that quietly structure contemporary civic life; from surveillance networks and algorithmic decision-making to the data infrastructures embedded within so-called “smart cities.” Rather than treating these systems as invisible background conditions, the exhibition brings them into public view, inviting visitors to consider their social, political, and ethical implications. The exhibition takes its title from French philosopher Gilles Deleuze’s concept of the “any-space-whatever,” a term later adapted by urban critic Adam Greenfield to describe the abstract, frictionless environments envisioned in corporate and policy-driven narratives of the smart city. title: Idris Murphy debuts unseen rare collection of three dimensional works
summary: Idris Murphy returns to Mitchell Fine Art in Fortitude Valley with intimate, three-dimensional works that invite us to look at the landscape in an entirely new way with his new exhibition opening from 8 September 2026. Bringing together two significant bodies of work, the exhibition presents a rare collection of 14 previously unseen dioramas alongside a new series of paintings inspired by the Australian outback. Alongside his paintings, these miniature constructions extend Murphy's ongoing exploration of place, memory, and the Australian landscape. Murphy’s paintings similarly move beyond conventional representations of landscape. Working en plein air, he seeks to capture the spirit of a place rather than its literal likeness. title: Friedrich Kunath debuts first solo exhibition with Pace in Seoul
summary: Pace will present The Nearest Faraway Place, a solo exhibition of new paintings and drawings by Friedrich Kunath. This marks the artist’s first solo exhibition with Pace in Seoul and his second exhibition since joining the gallery’s program in 2025. Across the exhibited works, Kunath explores themes of distance and (re)location, where a longing emerges between the place you're in and the place you're destined to be. Roads disappear around corners, over hills, and beyond horizons; figures are silhouetted by the sunsets they gaze upon, luring the spectator inward, toward themselves. As we look out onto the world, the world looks back at us, revealing our weaknesses and uncertainties. title: Boston College selected to present "Exercises in Empathy" global exhibition
summary: Boston College is among seven premier Catholic universities in major cities worldwide selected to host an exhibition on the theme of “Exercises in Empathy.” The exhibitions are part of a global contemporary art series launched by the Catholic Universities Art Triennial (“Art Cut”), commissioned by the Dicastery for Culture and Education of the Holy See. Boston College, the project’s exclusive North American venue, and one of three Jesuit Universities chosen to take part, will present “Art Cut: Exercises in Empathy: Accompaniment,” which opens on campus September 23 and runs through November 15 in the University’s Burns Library Board of Trustees Room. title: Kunstinstituut Melly to open major Moshekwa Langa survey exhibition
summary: On October 24, Kunstinstituut Melly will open You will find us in the best places, a major survey exhibition of South African artist Moshekwa Langa. Featuring nearly 120 works from the past three decades, the exhibition will occupy the entire building, making it the largest overview of Moshekwa’s work to be presented in the Netherlands, where he has lived for more than 25 years. Emerging in the early years of post-apartheid South Africa, Moshekwa belongs to a generation of artists who worked with the new enthusiasm sweeping through the country at the time and the curiosity toward a world that was opening up after decades of international solidarity through cultural sanctions and boycotts. title: William King Museum of Art to showcase fantasy art from the Korshak Collection
summary: The William King Museum of Art in Abingdon, Virginia will present an exhibition of selections from the Korshak Collection, on view September 28, 2026 through January 25, 2027. Featuring 57 works by artists including Frank Frazetta, Michael Whelan, the Brothers Hildebrandt, Arthur Rackham, Charles Vess, Hannes Bok, J. Allen St. John, and Brian Froud, among many others, the exhibition explores the rich visual worlds of fantasy and science fiction. Spanning the late nineteenth century through the early twentieth century, the works trace the evolution of imaginative realism and illustration, highlighting the enduring power of narrative art to bring myth, literature, and speculative worlds to life. title: National Asian Culture Center unveils 115-channel sound installation by YoungEun Kim
summary: The National Asian Culture Center presents To Future Listeners: Migrating Sounds, a new commission by YoungEun Kim, for the second edition of the ACC Future Prize. Awarded biennially, the prize recognizes promising artists working in interdisciplinary practices and supports the production and exhibition of new works. The exhibition explores the histories of movement and migration in Asia through sound, inviting visitors to experience them with the full range of their senses. Employing Wave Field Synthesis (WFS) and an immersive spatial audio system, it creates a multilayered soundscape in which diverse voices move, overlap, and resonate throughout the space. title: Museum Ludwig marks 50 years with free anniversary celebration in Cologne
summary: Fifty years after a landmark gift transformed Cologne’s cultural landscape, the Museum Ludwig is preparing to celebrate its anniversary with a full day of art, music, dance, workshops and free admission on Sunday, September 13, 2026. Founded in 1976 following the donation of an extraordinary collection by Peter and Irene Ludwig to the city of Cologne, the museum has grown into one of Europe’s most important institutions for modern and contemporary art. Its fiftieth anniversary offers an opportunity not only to celebrate that history, but also to consider how the museum—and the art it collects—has changed over the past half century. Today, the Museum Ludwig holds the largest collection of American Pop Art outside the United States as well as the world’s third-largest collection of works by Pablo Picasso. title: Matt Copson illuminates Fridericianum facade for Kassel Museum Night
summary: British artist Matt Copson has designed the site-specific work Flowers (2026) specially for this year's Kassel Museum Night. The temporary intervention consists of eight colorful laser projections illuminating the entire exterior facade of the Fridericianum. Using projectors typically found in clubs and stage productions, animated flowers bloom, wilt, and dissolve into abstraction in a constant loop. Together, their amorphous forms transform the building into an artificial landscape as the lasers continuously redraw lines of light through the darkness. The projection will be accompanied by an ambient score composed and performed live by British-Polish artist felicita, adding an auditory dimension to the installation.
